14 Two coplanar forces act on the rim of a wheel. The forces are equal in magnitude.
Which arrangement of forces provides only a couple?
A
B
C
D

hints: Look at the directions of the two equal forces on the rim in each diagram and check whether the vector sum can be zero.
Recall a couple needs two equal and opposite parallel forces, so resultant $F - F = 0$ but the moments about the centre add.
Compare diagrams B, C and A for a non-zero resultant, then check the remaining opposite parallel pair for separation that gives torque $F \times d$ with no net force.
walkthrough: Identify the condition for only a couple: two forces must be equal in magnitude, parallel, and opposite in direction, giving zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant moment.
Check A and C: the arrows are at $90$ degrees to each other, so they cannot cancel to zero resultant force and must give both translation and rotation.
Check B: both arrows point to the right at top and bottom of the wheel, so resultant is the sum, not zero, and there is a net force.
Check D: top arrow points right and bottom arrow points left with equal magnitude, so resultant force $= F + (-F) = 0$.

Both forces in D produce a moment in the same rotational sense about the centre, with moment $= F \times d$ where $d$ is the wheel diameter, so there is pure turning with no translation. This is option D.

A.explanation: The two forces are perpendicular, one up and one to the right, so the vector sum is not zero and there is a resultant force.

B.explanation: The two forces are parallel in the same direction, so the resultant force is $2F$ and the wheel would translate as well as turn.

C.explanation: The two forces are perpendicular, one right and one down, so the resultant force is not zero and it is not a couple.

D.explanation: The two forces are equal, opposite and parallel with separation equal to the wheel diameter, so resultant force is zero and only a turning moment remains.
